title: The Burnt Debt
premise: Odile Vane, a financial-crimes investigator who once laundered money for the Meridian syndicate before turning state's witness, has spent five years hiding behind clean ledgers and a polished lie. When a burner phone rings with the voice of her presumed-dead handler, Tomas, she learns Meridian is using her old laundering architecture to move funds for an attack disguised as an industrial accident at the Verrin checkpoint. Hunted by both the syndicate and a colleague who suspects her past, Odile must rebuild trust with the found family she abandoned—her former crew—to trace the money and stop the attack before the border shift change. In the end, she burns the debt for good: she exposes Meridian, loses Tomas a second time, and chooses truth over invisibility, surrendering to testify rather than run.
about_author: Zephyrine Zhou is a former compliance analyst who traded spreadsheet forensics for fiction after a decade tracing money across three continents. She writes thrillers about people whose lies are load-bearing, from a harbor apartment full of half-packed suitcases.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. We meet her meticulous double life: flawless investigator by day, go-bag by the door, rehearsed cover story by night. A routine audit of shell companies snags on a structure she recognizes as her own five-year-old handiwork. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing your buried past is surfacing.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The burner phone in her emergency kit—registered to a dead man—rings. Tomas's voice: he's alive, he needs her, and the call traces back through her own laundering network. She hangs up, then can't stop shaking. Emotional beat: terror braided with longing for the family she betrayed.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Odile and Marcus Iyer, her sharp-eyed colleague pulling threads on the same shells. Odile realizes the money flows toward the Verrin border checkpoint and a scheduled 'maintenance' window. Marcus notices her recognition a beat too fast. Emotional beat: paranoia—the hunter sensing she might be prey.

chapters.title: Old Crew, New Graves
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She tracks down Sefa, her former crew's forger, now living quiet under another name. Sefa refuses until Odile admits what she did to them all: testified, scattered their lives, vanished. Emotional beat: guilt made flesh; the first crack in her polished lie.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa lays out what Meridian owes each of them—and what Odile owes. Together they decode the payment pattern: the attack is funded through a charity foundation, timed to the checkpoint shift change when staffing thins. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; found family reassembling around shared damage.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knows
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Iyer confronts Odile privately—he's found her old alias in sealed testimony files. Instead of arresting her, he offers a deal: help him stop the attack, and he'll bury her past. Emotional beat: the terrifying relief of being seen and not condemned.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She meets Tomas face to face in a freight yard—and discovers his 'rescue' was bait: Meridian knew she'd come, and the attack intel is partly a trap to flush out the traitor. He claims he's protecting her. She stops believing him mid-sentence. Emotional beat: heartbreak hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Follow the Burn
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The crew plus Marcus race the clock: freeze the foundation's accounts, map the 'accident' mechanism—a gas-line override at the checkpoint canteen—and realize the trigger requires credentials only someone inside Meridian holds. Tomas's. Emotional beat: desperate momentum, every plan fraying at the edges.

chapters.title: Verrin
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax. At the checkpoint, Odile talks Tomas down over the open line while Sefa kills the override and Marcus evacuates the night shift. Tomas hesitates—then triggers it anyway, and dies in the blast he meant to shrink to nothing. Emotional beat: love, betrayal, and grief colliding in ninety seconds.

chapters.title: The Polished Lie, Retired
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, resolution. The attack is framed as foiled terrorism; Meridian's finances unravel under Marcus's case. Odile unpacks the go-bag, then repacks it one last time—not to flee, but to walk into headquarters and give a full statement under her real name. Emotional beat: quiet, costly peace; loyalty finally aligned with truth.
